newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Hydro yr profits, sales volumes up.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Hydro yr profits, sales volumes up.

text.p: British electricity generator Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc said on Thursday that the current financial year had started well with a further increase in sales volume.

The company, which reported a 5.3 percent rise in pretax profits to 205.4 million pounds ($335.4 million) and paid a final dividend of 12.36 pence per share, added that investments would raise gearing to around 65 percent by 1999 from 52.1 percent currently.

Scottish Hydro said interest cover should fall to around six times by 1999 but added that by allowing this to fall further, it had the capacity to invest in "substantial projects when the conditions are right."
It said it aimed to continue producing "significant real dividend growth," and was prepared to reduce "modestly" its present level of dividend cover over the next few years to achieve this.

The company, which bought out United Utilities, its 50 percent partner in the Keadby power station, for 122.7 million pounds in February, said it expected to hold eight percent of the British generation market by 1999, when new plants would be completed.

Scottish Hydro said it was working on plans to take advantage of liberalisation of the domestic electricity supply market in 1998, adding that it was "confident that our efficient power system and our portfolio of...plant can succeed over the medium term in delivering attractive returns to shareholders." ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
